content:
We have docs#Ideal.under which is an abbrev for the contraction of an ideal given [Algebra A B], i.e. Ideal.under A P = Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B). There are currently 55 usages in mathlib. Conversely, there are 85 hits for Ideal.comap (algebraMap ?R ?A).

In #37840, @Thomas Browning is proposing to replace some more usages of Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) by Ideal.under.

  • It leads to some additional rewriting with Ideal.under_def in places where we want to apply the general API for Ideal.comap and my personal experience with Ideal.under has been that I usually want to rewrite with Ideal.under_def as soon as possible to get the generic form.
  • On the other hand, Ideal.under A P is quite a bit shorter than Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B).

I think we should either:

  • get rid of Ideal.under
  • use Ideal.under everywhere and go forward with #37840 (then there are two options: live with the additional Ideal.under_def rewriting or duplicate a bunch of API for Ideal.comap)
  • replace Ideal.under by notation (in that case, I don't know if it is possible to still make it work with dot notation?)

What do people prefer?
Personally I have found Ideal.under to be quite ergonomic, but of course the duplication of API is not ideal.
Do we actually need to duplicate API given that this is an abbrev? I thought the point of abbrevs was that you didn't have to do so

Eric Wieser said:

This is analogous to docs#Submodule.submoduleOf, right?

Yes, but Submodule.submoduleOf is not even an abbrev.

Eric Wieser said:

Do we actually need to duplicate API given that this is an abbrev? I thought the point of abbrevs was that you didn't have to do so

Yes because rw does not see through abbrevs.
